title: Europe’s Broad Earnings Recovery
gist: Teaser excerpt only (the article is cut at 'Want to read the whole article?' after two paragraphs): Gavekal argues European equities are a way to keep AI exposure without owning the fragility of the AI earnings boom, because Europe's earnings recovery is diversified across sectors. The one hard number given is consensus 12-month forward EPS growth for MSCI Europe of 15.4% in euro terms at end-July 2026, versus a -2% contraction in July 2025.

themes.theme: European equities as a hedged AI trade

insights.claim: Investors who doubt the sustainability of the AI earnings boom but still want AI exposure should look at European equities, which offer a powerful earnings-recovery story with a significant AI element.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Frames European equity exposure as a way to stay long the AI theme with less single-theme drawdown risk than US AI leaders.
insights.quote: Investors who question the sustainability of the AI earnings boom, but who nevertheless want to retain some exposure to the growth of artificial intelligence, may want to look again at European equities.

insights.claim: Europe's earnings growth is diversified across a broad range of sectors and therefore stands a good chance of surviving even if the AI boom turns to bust.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The durability argument rests on breadth, not on AI beta — so watch sector dispersion of European EPS revisions as the thing that would falsify the call.

insights.claim: Breadth of earnings growth across sectors — rather than exposure to the dominant growth theme itself — is the criterion for judging which equity markets survive an AI bust.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Gives a screenable test for AI-bust resilience: measure how concentrated a market's forward EPS growth is in AI-linked sectors.

insights.claim: At the end of July 2026, consensus estimates projected 12-month forward earnings-per-share growth for the MSCI Europe index of 15.4% measured in euro terms, versus a -2% contraction in July 2025.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A ~17-point year-on-year swing in forward EPS growth is the quantitative spine of the European re-rating case; track whether the 15.4% consensus holds or gets revised down.
